subject: sociology
title: Ownership, Bias and Bobo Dolls
welcome_lead: Who owns the news, and does watching violence make us violent? Apply key studies to ownership and effects.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure applying Curran & Seaton, GMG and Bandura to media ownership and effects.
final_note: Pair every claim with a named theorist or study to lock in AO2 marks.

concepts.def: Who controls the production of media content.
Ownership in fewer hands, e.g. Murdoch group.

Researchers showing TV news has built-in bias.
Becoming numb to violence after heavy exposure.

walkthroughs.body_html: Curran and Seaton argue UK media ownership is highly concentrated. A few owners shape the news agenda to protect business interests, leaving little space for radical viewpoints.

Pluralists reply that the internet has multiplied voices. Bloggers, YouTubers and citizen journalists provide variety. Audiences choose freely, so owners cannot dictate ideas as simply as Marxists claim.
Bandura (1961) showed children copying adults who hit an inflatable Bobo doll on film. This supports the hypodermic syringe. Critics say a lab is not real life and children know dolls are not people.
